title: Polynomial Arithmetic Atlas: annotated reference collection
scope: Selective annotated research bibliography; primarily univariate polynomials over Q and number fields, with connected branches.

references.title: Local Fields
references.annotation: Treats valuations, ramification, the different, and discriminants. These provide the local field framework for Newton polygons and for constructing inertia elements in polynomial Galois groups.
references.note: English translation of Corps locaux by Marvin Jay Greenberg.

references.title: Finite Fields
references.annotation: Treats irreducible and primitive polynomials over finite fields, factorization, and constructions. An irreducible polynomial of degree n over a finite field has cyclic splitting-field group of order n; Galois groups over the rationals need not be cyclic.
references.series: Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications
references.metadata_note: The standard bibliographic year is 1997 (BNF and AMS review); the Cambridge product page lists a 24 October 1996 release date.

references.title: Algebraic Number Theory
references.annotation: Treats prime decomposition, ramification, and the global arithmetic of splitting fields, relating reduction modulo primes to arithmetic properties of number fields.
references.note: Translated from German by Norbert Schappacher.

references.title: Polynomials with Special Regard to Reducibility
references.annotation: Treats arbitrary and lacunary polynomials over several classes of fields. Its bibliography documents the classical literature on reducibility.
references.series: Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications
references.metadata_note: The monograph treats several broad field classes. Its publisher explicitly excludes results valid only over finite fields, local fields, or the rational field; use it together with field-specific references.

references.title: Algebra
references.annotation: Develops the algebra of irreducibility, field extensions, and Galois theory over general fields, including the distinction between separability and irreducibility.

references.title: Polynomials
references.annotation: Treats irreducibility on pp. 47–76, special polynomial forms on pp. 77–131, and Galois theory on pp. 181–218, relating algebraic arguments to root location and explicit constructions.
references.metadata_note: The English first edition is ©2004 (hardcover published 9 July 2004); the linked eBook was released 23 September 2009. These are editions/formats of the same book.

references.title: Galois Theory
references.annotation: Develops field extensions and explicit Galois-group calculations through worked examples. Chapters 13 and 14 treat resolvents, computation, and solvable permutation groups.

references.title: Fields and Galois Theory
references.annotation: Develops field and Galois theory through proofs and examples; Chapter 4 treats Galois-group computation. The linked file is the 2022 book. The author’s errata address, among other points, irreducibility in Q[X] versus Z[X] and the degree-two exception in polynomial counting. The frozen course notes v5.10 have different pagination.
references.metadata_note: Author errata: https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/fterrata.html. Course-note version 5.10 is frozen; the author directs readers to the book for corrections and updates.

references.title: Von denjenigen Moduln, welche Potenzen von Primzahlen sind. (Fortsetzung)
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
references.annotation: Precedes Eisenstein’s treatment of the criterion now often called Schönemann–Eisenstein. Cox’s historical account explains the role of higher congruences and translates the statement into modern polynomial language.

references.title: Über die Irreductibilität und einige andere Eigenschaften der Gleichung, von welcher die Theilung der ganzen Lemniscate abhängt
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
references.annotation: Develops Eisenstein’s criterion in connection with division of the lemniscate and Gaussian integers. For an integer polynomial, the familiar criterion requires a prime dividing every nonleading coefficient but not the leading coefficient, with its square not dividing the constant coefficient.

references.title: Sulla riduttibilità della funzione x^n-A in un campo qualunque di razionalità
references.annotation: Classical reference for the binomial irreducibility criterion, including the exceptional fourth-power obstruction when the exponent is divisible by four. Distinguish this binomial criterion from the related Capelli composition lemma; the note itself points back to Capelli's 1897 and 1898 work.

references.title: Sur quelques cas d'irréductibilité des polynômes à coefficients rationnels
references.venue: Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées, 6e série
references.annotation: Uses Newton polygons to restrict possible factor degrees. In the one-edge case, coprime horizontal and vertical increments give an irreducibility criterion; the polygon-product rule applies to more general factorization questions.

references.title: Neue Kriterien für die Irreduzibilität algebraischer Gleichungen
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
references.annotation: Classical criteria based on coefficient dominance and the location of complex roots. A standard application is a monic integer polynomial with nonzero constant term and next-to-leading coefficient larger in absolute value than one plus the sum of the lower coefficient magnitudes.

references.title: Problem 226
references.annotation: Original question on products of distinct integral linear factors perturbed by ±1. The link is to the later historical account that verifies this citation, rather than to a scan of the original problem; that account also records Schur's Problem275 (1909) on power compositions.
references.metadata_note: The main link identifies Győry–Hajdu–Tijdeman (2011), the later source used to verify the historical citation, rather than an original scan.

references.title: Verschiedene Bemerkungen zur Zahlentheorie
references.annotation: Original source for irreducibility criteria obtained from sufficiently small nonzero values at many distinct integers. The interpolation argument and later improvements are developed in Levit1968, Tverberg1973 and Győry–Hajdu–Tijdeman2011.

references.title: Zur Theorie der Irreduzibilitätskriterien
references.annotation: Extends valuation-based irreducibility criteria beyond the Eisenstein and Dumas cases, preceding the development of augmented valuations and higher-order Newton polygons.
references.metadata_note: DOI, volume 18, pages 278–288, and December 1923 publication date checked against the publisher. The original 1922 date is the received date, not the publication year.

references.authors: Dorwart, H. L. and Ore, Øystein
references.title: Criteria for the irreducibility of polynomials
references.annotation: Studies irreducibility from repeated small or prime values at integer arguments and extends Schur-type constructions involving products of linear factors.

references.title: Irreducibility of polynomials
references.annotation: Surveys classical criteria based on coefficient divisibility, coefficient size, and values at integers. Its bibliography records the literature available at the time.

references.title: A construction for absolute values in polynomial rings
references.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Constructs polynomial valuations through successive augmentations and key polynomials. This framework supports irreducibility tests beyond a first Newton polygon and underlies modern local factorization methods.

references.title: On the reducibility of polynomials and in particular of trinomials
references.annotation: Studies structural reducibility, especially for sparse polynomials and trinomials. Specific statements should be read with the 1966 errata.

references.title: Errata to the paper "On the reducibility of polynomials and in particular of trinomials"
references.annotation: Corrects statements in Schinzel’s 1965 paper; the correction and original paper should be consulted together.

references.title: Irreducibility of polynomials with low absolute values
references.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Sharpens the interpolation bounds in Pólya’s small-value criterion. Its exclusions of factors of specified degrees can be combined with local degree restrictions.

references.title: On the irreducibility of polynomials taking small values
references.annotation: Refines the small-value method, including asymptotic bounds, extending the interpolation arguments of Pólya and Levit.

references.authors: Brillhart, John and Filaseta, Michael and Odlyzko, Andrew
references.title: On an irreducibility theorem of A. Cohn
references.annotation: Generalizes the criterion that a prime’s digit expansion gives an irreducible polynomial when its digits are used as coefficients. It identifies coefficient restrictions under which a single prime evaluation proves irreducibility.

references.authors: Khanduja, Sudesh K. and Saha, Jayanti
references.title: On a generalization of Eisenstein's irreducibility criterion
references.annotation: Extends the Eisenstein method over valued fields to coefficient patterns beyond the ordinary divisibility criterion.

references.title: On the factorization of polynomials with small Euclidean norm
references.annotation: Uses the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector to constrain factorization, including that of sparse polynomials and their nonreciprocal parts. Irreducibility of the nonreciprocal part does not imply irreducibility of the whole polynomial.
references.metadata_note: Pages143–163 follow the author's bibliography and MathSciNet citation reproduced in Sawin–Shusterman–Stoll; the publisher chapter wrapper gives143–164, apparently including a trailing page.

references.authors: Filaseta, Michael and Ford, Kevin and Konyagin, Sergei
references.title: On an irreducibility theorem of A. Schinzel associated with coverings of the integers
references.annotation: For large exponents, controls the nonreciprocal part of f(x)x^n+g(x), assuming coprimality, nonzero constant terms of both f and g, and explicit Capelli-type exclusions. The method improves the threshold in Schinzel's theorem and connects sparse factorization to covering systems.

references.title: Prime numbers and irreducible polynomials
references.annotation: Relates prime values, coefficient bounds, and irreducibility, with Cohn’s theorem as an example. A single prime value requires additional size or coefficient hypotheses; the paper states such hypotheses.

references.title: Irreducibility of polynomials whose coefficients are integers
references.annotation: Surveys classical tests for rational irreducibility of integer polynomials and explains their limitations.
references.metadata_note: The author’s bibliography confirms RMS Mathematical Newsletter 17(2) (2007), 29–37. A distinct 2009 chapter with the same title is coauthored with N. Saradha.

references.title: Why Eisenstein Proved the Eisenstein Criterion and Why Schönemann Discovered It First
references.annotation: Explains the history and mathematics of Eisenstein’s criterion through Gauss’s lemma, finite fields, Hensel lifting, Gaussian integers, and lemniscatic division. It distinguishes the arguments and contributions of Schönemann and Eisenstein.
references.metadata_note: The cited Monthly version (2011), pp. 3–21, is a reprint with minor changes of the article in Normat 57(2) (2009), pp. 49–73; the Monthly first-page footnote explicitly acknowledges the earlier publication. Publisher online migration date 13 December 2017 is not the publication year.

references.authors: Győry, Kálmán and Hajdu, Lajos and Tijdeman, Robert
references.title: Irreducibility criteria of Schur-type and Pólya-type
references.annotation: Research paper with a substantial historical introduction and bibliography on small-value criteria, perturbed products and compositions. Its extensions use interpolation, algebraic number theory and Diophantine approximation, including results over imaginary quadratic rings and compositions of CM type.

references.title: Schönemann–Eisenstein–Dumas-type irreducibility conditions that use arbitrarily many prime numbers
references.annotation: Combines coefficient divisibility at several primes through Newton polygons. Intersecting the permitted factor degrees can exclude every proper factor even when each prime alone is inconclusive.
references.metadata_note: Published in 2015; open author preprint v2 dated 21 March 2014. Theorem A gives the several-prime factor-degree intersection criterion. The former secondary verification link DOI 10.1090/proc/14856 is replaced by this paper’s own primary text.

references.authors: Cole, Morgan and Dunn, Scott and Filaseta, Michael
references.title: Further irreducibility criteria for polynomials with non-negative coefficients
references.annotation: Continues the Cohn prime-value approach for nonnegative integer coefficients. It determines sharp coefficient bounds for bases from 3 through 20, allowing coefficients larger than ordinary base digits while retaining an irreducibility conclusion from a prime evaluation.

references.authors: Filaseta, Michael and Li, Huixi and Patane, Frank and Skabelund, Dane
references.title: On the irreducibility of the non-reciprocal part of polynomials of the form f(x)x^n+g(x)
references.annotation: Improves the sufficient exponent threshold in the robust-pair method of Sawin, Shusterman and Stoll. The conclusion concerns the nonreciprocal part, so reciprocal factors still require separate analysis when proving full irreducibility.

references.authors: Sawin, Will and Shusterman, Mark and Stoll, Michael
references.title: Irreducibility of polynomials with a large gap
references.annotation: Develops Ljunggren’s factor-reversal method into irreducibility algorithms for x^N c(x^-1)+d(x). It treats cyclotomic obstructions separately, improves effective bounds under additional robustness hypotheses, and reviews earlier large-gap results.

references.title: Théorèmes sur les groupes primitifs
references.venue: Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées (2)
references.annotation: Establishes primitive-group results used to prove containment of A_n in polynomial Galois groups. Modern expositions give the prime-cycle criterion in current terminology, including its primitivity hypothesis.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods

references.authors: Dixon, John D. and Mortimer, Brian
references.title: Permutation Groups
references.annotation: Treats transitivity, block systems, primitive groups, and Jordan-type criteria for large permutation groups. These criteria apply once modular factorization or local ramification has supplied cycle information.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods

references.authors: Stevenhagen, Peter and Lenstra, Jr., Hendrik W.
references.title: Chebotarëv and his density theorem
references.annotation: Explains Frobenius conjugacy classes and their relation to splitting modulo primes, with the history and proof of Chebotarev’s theorem. It describes what modular factorization data can establish and what remains undetermined.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods

references.title: Primitive permutation groups containing a cycle
references.venue: Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Classifies primitive finite permutation groups containing a cycle and strengthens Jordan’s prime-cycle theorem. Theorems 1.1–1.2 and Corollary 1.3 justify the cycle criteria used here. Prefer the published version: Remark 1.9 corrects the older preprint’s distinction between polynomial composition and primitivity of a fixed polynomial’s root action.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods
references.metadata_note: Published online 18 July 2013; journal issue February 2014. Use the published text: preprint Comments 1 and 3 became Remarks 1.4 and 1.6, and the inaccurate fixed-polynomial indecomposability claim in arXiv v1 Comment 6 was corrected to a divisibility criterion in published Remark 1.9.

references.authors: Lagarias, Jeffrey C. and Odlyzko, Andrew M.
references.title: Effective versions of the Chebotarev density theorem
references.venue: Algebraic Number Fields: L-functions and Galois Properties (Proc. Sympos., Univ. Durham, Durham, 1975)
references.annotation: Gives conditional and unconditional effective Chebotarev estimates. These bound the primes with specified Frobenius conjugacy classes.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods
references.metadata_note: The main link is Lagarias’s bibliography, which verifies the 1977 proceedings chapter (pp. 409–464); it is not a full-text link.

references.title: The Distribution of Galois Groups and Hilbert's Irreducibility Theorem
references.venue: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (3)
references.annotation: Gives quantitative bounds for exceptional specializations and Galois-group distributions in polynomial families by combining Hilbert irreducibility with sieve estimates.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods

references.title: Quelques applications du théorème de densité de Chebotarev
references.annotation: Develops effective Chebotarev estimates and arithmetic applications, specifying the dependence on analytic hypotheses, extension degrees, and discriminants.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods

references.title: A unified and improved Chebotarev density theorem
references.annotation: Gives an unconditional effective Chebotarev theorem with improved uniformity, including a possible exceptional zero. Its parameter dependence determines when an unconditional estimate can replace a GRH-based estimate in a probabilistic or computational argument.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods

references.title: On the irreducibility of certain trinomials
references.section: Special families: trinomials and sparse families
references.annotation: Proves irreducibility of x^n-x-1 over Q for every n at least 2. The later full symmetric-group conclusion has a separate attribution.

references.title: On the irreducibility of certain trinomials and quadrinomials
references.section: Special families: trinomials and sparse families
references.annotation: Studies factorization of sparse polynomials through the distinction between reciprocal and nonreciprocal factors. Its factor-reversal method extends to later large-gap problems.

references.title: Equations of the type X^n+aX+b with absolute Galois group S_n
references.venue: Revista de la Universidad de Santander
references.section: Special families: trinomials and sparse families
references.annotation: An early source for symmetric Galois groups of trinomials; in particular, it precedes Osada for x^n-x-1. The institutional catalogue supplies an English title although the original paper is in Spanish.

references.title: The Galois groups of the polynomials X^n+aX^l+b
references.section: Special families: trinomials and sparse families
references.annotation: Gives arithmetic conditions forcing the full symmetric group for trinomials, using ramification to obtain transpositions. It includes an independent proof for x^n-x-1.

references.authors: Cohen, Stephen D. and Movahhedi, A. and Salinier, Alain
references.title: Double transitivity of Galois groups of trinomials
references.section: Special families: trinomials and sparse families
references.annotation: Studies how arithmetic hypotheses on a trinomial force double transitivity. This is an intermediate group-theoretic step that can be combined with cycle or ramification information to obtain a large Galois group.

references.authors: Cohen, Stephen D. and Movahhedi, A. and Salinier, Alain
references.title: Galois groups of trinomials
references.section: Special families: trinomials and sparse families
references.annotation: Extends earlier results of Osada using primitivity, cycle structure, and arithmetic restrictions. Apply the precise irreducibility and coprimality assumptions in the paper rather than treating sparsity alone as a sufficient condition.

references.title: Einige Sätze über Primzahlen mit Anwendungen auf Irreduzibilitätsfragen, I
references.venue: Sitzungsberichte der Preußischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Physikalisch-Mathematische Klasse
references.section: Special families: Schur and orthogonal polynomials
references.annotation: Classical prime-divisor arguments applied to irreducibility. Read alongside Part II and the 1930/1931 papers to trace the origin of factorial-coefficient and orthogonal-polynomial methods.
references.status: Published; citation verified through later literature
references.metadata_note: The linked source is Rabarison–Pazuki–Molin (2024), bibliography entry [20], which verifies the original citation. It is not a scan of Schur’s 1929 paper.

references.title: Gleichungen ohne Affekt
references.venue: Sitzungsberichte der Preußischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Physikalisch-Mathematische Klasse
references.section: Special families: Schur and orthogonal polynomials
references.annotation: Proves the Galois-group theorem for exponential Taylor polynomials. Coleman later gives a proof using Newton polygons.
references.status: Published; citation verified through later literature
references.metadata_note: The linked source is Rabarison–Pazuki–Molin (2024), bibliography entry [22], which verifies the original citation. It is not a scan of Schur’s 1930 paper.

references.title: Affektlose Gleichungen in der Theorie der Laguerreschen und Hermiteschen Polynome
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
references.section: Special families: Schur and orthogonal polynomials
references.annotation: Studies irreducibility and Galois groups of Laguerre and Hermite polynomials. Statements for Hermite polynomials must account for parity and the forced factor at zero.

references.title: On the Galois groups of the exponential Taylor polynomials
references.section: Special families: Taylor and truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: Proves Schur’s theorem for sum_{j=0}^n x^j/j!: irreducible over Q, with group A_n when 4 divides n and S_n otherwise (n at least 2). The proof combines Newton-polygon slopes, long cycles, and the discriminant square test.

references.title: The Galois group of x^n-x^{n-1}-...-x-1
references.venue: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra
references.section: Special families: Taylor and truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: Proves that the generalized Fibonacci polynomial has group S_n when n is even or prime. The prime-degree argument includes irreducibility of its reduction modulo that prime.

references.authors: Filaseta, Michael and Kumchev, Angel and Pasechnik, Dmitrii
references.title: On the irreducibility of a truncated binomial expansion
references.section: Special families: Taylor and truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: Studies irreducibility of the first k+1 terms of (1+x)^n and related coefficient families through factorial-coefficient criteria.

references.title: The theorem of Jentzsch--Szegő on an analytic curve: application to the irreducibility of truncations of power series
references.section: Special families: Taylor and truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: Relates zero-distribution on analytic curves, including nonarchimedean curves, to irreducibility information for truncations. Use the corrected published version or arXiv v3; the arXiv history specifically records a correction to the application.

references.title: On the Galois group over Q of a truncated binomial expansion
references.section: Special families: Taylor and truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: For a fixed truncation degree r other than 6, proves that sufficiently large n gives S_r for the first r+1 terms of (1+x)^n. At r=6 it bounds the number of exceptions n up to N by O(log N).

references.authors: Shokri, Khosro Monsef and Shaffaf, Jafar and Taleb, Reza
references.title: Galois groups of Taylor polynomials of some elementary functions
references.section: Special families: Taylor and truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: Studies truncations associated with logarithmic and cosine functions. The cosine examples naturally involve a signed-permutation group because of their even symmetry.

references.authors: Rabarison, Patrick and Pazuki, Fabien and Molin, Pascal
references.title: Exponentielle tronquée et autres contes galoisiens
references.venue: Publications mathématiques de Besançon. Algèbre et théorie des nombres
references.section: Special families: Taylor and truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: Surveys exponential truncations and gives explicit investigations of Padé approximants, relating Schur’s classical results to later computational questions.

references.authors: Katz, Nicholas M. and Rivin, Igor
references.title: Speculations in Galois Theory
references.section: Special families: Taylor and truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: Poses limiting-frequency questions for Galois groups of Taylor truncations and reports computations in many families. The note explicitly separates experimental evidence from theorems; its posted copy has no date on the title page.
references.status: Author-hosted contribution to the Laumon volume; publication year not verified

references.title: Bessel Polynomials
references.section: Special families: Laguerre and Bessel polynomials
references.annotation: Treats Bessel polynomials, including their algebraic irreducibility and Galois groups. Its irreducibility conjecture was later resolved by Filaseta and Trifonov.

references.title: On the irreducibility of the generalized Laguerre polynomials
references.section: Special families: Laguerre and Bessel polynomials
references.annotation: For each fixed rational parameter outside the negative integers, proves irreducibility over Q in every sufficiently large degree. The threshold depends on the parameter, so this is not a uniform theorem when the parameter varies with degree.

references.title: The irreducibility of the Bessel polynomials
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
references.section: Special families: Laguerre and Bessel polynomials
references.annotation: Resolves Grosswald’s irreducibility conjecture for Bessel polynomials in every positive degree. Proves a stronger coefficient-perturbation statement using Newton polygons and prime-divisor estimates.

references.title: On the Galois group of generalized Laguerre polynomials
references.venue: Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux
references.section: Special families: Laguerre and Bessel polynomials
references.annotation: Introduces a Newton-index criterion for containing A_n and applies it, together with irreducibility results, to generalized Laguerre polynomials with fixed rational parameter outside the negative integers in sufficiently large degree. Irreducibility is an explicit input to the group criterion.

references.title: Algebraic properties of a family of generalized Laguerre polynomials
references.section: Special families: Laguerre and Bessel polynomials
references.annotation: Studies negative integral parameters linked to degree, a regime different from the fixed-parameter theorem. Newton polygons organize irreducibility and large-group results, together with precise remaining conjectures.

references.authors: Filaseta, Michael and Kidd, Travis and Trifonov, Ognian
references.title: Laguerre polynomials with Galois group A_m for each m
references.section: Special families: Laguerre and Bessel polynomials
references.annotation: Completes Schur's generalized Laguerre realizations of A_m by treating m congruent to 2 modulo 4. The constructed polynomials are irreducible for m > 2, while m = 2 is the split case.

references.authors: Banerjee, Pradipto and Filaseta, Michael and Finch, Carrie E. and Leidy, J. Russell
references.title: On classifying Laguerre polynomials which have Galois group the alternating group
references.venue: Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux
references.section: Special families: Laguerre and Bessel polynomials
references.annotation: Classifies the integer parameter pairs with nonzero square discriminant into explicit infinite families and a finite remainder. A square discriminant constrains the group to A_n but does not by itself prove irreducibility or equality with A_n.

references.title: Families of Laguerre polynomials with alternating group as Galois group
references.section: Special families: Laguerre and Bessel polynomials
references.annotation: Proves irreducibility and group results for integer parameters in the interval [-2n-4,-2n], including Bessel-related cases. Verifies parts of the alternating-group conjectural classification in that range.

references.authors: Cullinan, John and Hajir, Farshid and Sell, Elizabeth
references.title: Algebraic properties of a family of Jacobi polynomials
references.venue: Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux
references.section: Special families: Jacobi, Legendre and related polynomials
references.annotation: For fixed n at least 6, obtains irreducibility for all but finitely many rational parameters in a particular one-parameter Jacobi subfamily. The Galois-group exceptional set is finite for odd n and thin for even n.

references.title: On the Galois groups of Legendre polynomials
references.section: Special families: Jacobi, Legendre and related polynomials
references.annotation: Studies the groups of parity-reduced Legendre polynomials through discriminants and Newton polygons. Its results and conjectures must be stated for the correct reduced polynomial, with irreducibility assumptions where required.

references.title: Algebraic properties of Kaneko-Zagier lifts of supersingular polynomials
references.venue: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
references.section: Special families: Jacobi, Legendre and related polynomials
references.annotation: Connects rational lifts of supersingular polynomials with specialized Jacobi polynomials. Gives new irreducibility cases and investigates the Mahlburg–Ono maximal-Galois-group conjecture after removing trivial factors.

references.title: On the irreducibility of the Krawtchouck polynomials
references.venue: Journal of the Ramanujan Mathematical Society
references.section: Special families: Jacobi, Legendre and related polynomials
references.annotation: Determines Newton polygons for certain Krawtchouck polynomials and uses them to prove new irreducibility cases.

references.title: Note on irreducibility of the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials
references.annotation: An early arithmetic source for irreducibility in Bernoulli and Euler families. These are the Appell polynomials defined by exponential generating functions, and should not be conflated with descent-enumerating Eulerian polynomials.

references.title: On the Euler and Bernoulli polynomials
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials
references.annotation: Studies factorization and roots of Euler and Bernoulli polynomials, including irreducibility results and normalizations after removing forced factors.

references.title: Théorie géométrique des polynômes eulériens
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials
references.annotation: Develops the conventions, generating functions, and symmetries of Eulerian polynomials used in their arithmetic study.
references.metadata_note: The linked December 2005 TeX retypesetting is authorized; it reproduces the 1970 monograph with different pagination.

references.authors: Sharma, A. and Straus, Ernst G.
references.title: On the irreducibility of a class of Euler Frobenius polynomials
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials
references.annotation: Proves irreducibility results for Euler–Frobenius polynomials. Theorem 6 at parameter r=1 includes the classical Eulerian polynomial at an odd prime index, where a shift gives Eisenstein’s criterion.

references.authors: Mináč, Ján and Nguyen, Tung T. and Tân, Nguyen Duy
references.title: Fekete polynomials, quadratic residues, and arithmetic
references.section: Special families: Fekete and reciprocal polynomials
references.annotation: Introduces normalized reciprocal and trace polynomials associated with prime-conductor Fekete polynomials, relates values to class numbers, and studies their splitting fields. The proposed full wreath-product group is a conjecture in this source, not an all-prime theorem.

references.authors: Mináč, Ján and Nguyen, Tung T. and Tân, Nguyen Duy
references.title: On the arithmetic of generalized Fekete polynomials
references.section: Special families: Fekete and reciprocal polynomials
references.annotation: Extends the arithmetic investigation to quadratic characters with possibly composite conductor. Cyclotomic factors, trace-polynomial reductions, and extra symmetries constrain the possible Galois groups.

references.authors: Anderson, Theresa C. and Bertelli, Adam and O'Dorney, Evan M.
references.title: Galois groups of reciprocal polynomials and the van der Waerden-Bhargava theorem
references.section: Special families: Fekete and reciprocal polynomials
references.annotation: For separable reciprocal polynomials of degree 2n and growing coefficient height H, gives exceptional proportion of order H^(-1) log H for nonmonic n ≥ 1 and monic n ≥ 3. The corrected version leaves the monic quartic case open; the expected group is the full signed-permutation group.

references.title: Die Seltenheit der reduziblen Gleichungen und der Gleichungen mit Affekt
references.section: Counting by height and probabilistic Galois theory
references.annotation: Studies the rarity of reducible polynomials and exceptional Galois groups in coefficient boxes as coefficient height grows with degree fixed.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Reducible polynomials
references.venue: Journal of the London Mathematical Society
references.section: Counting by height and probabilistic Galois theory
references.annotation: Gives asymptotic counts of reducible integer polynomials in fixed-degree coefficient boxes, including the main contribution from linear factors. Reducibility is distinct from having an exceptional transitive Galois group.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: The large sieve and probabilistic Galois theory
references.section: Counting by height and probabilistic Galois theory
references.annotation: Uses the large sieve to combine factorization information at many primes and bound exceptional Galois groups in fixed-degree integer coefficient boxes.
references.series: Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: On the distribution of Galois groups
references.section: Counting by height and probabilistic Galois theory
references.annotation: Bounds the number of monic integer polynomials of fixed degree and bounded height with a prescribed Galois group, using resolvents and integral-point estimates.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Enumerative Galois theory for cubics and quartics
references.section: Counting by height and probabilistic Galois theory
references.annotation: Studies counts for individual Galois groups in degrees three and four, refining the question of how often the full symmetric group occurs.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Bary-Soroker, Lior and Ben-Porath, Or and Matei, Vlad
references.title: Probabilistic Galois Theory: The square discriminant case
references.section: Counting by height and probabilistic Galois theory
references.annotation: Studies the frequency of alternating Galois groups and nonzero square discriminants in the fixed-degree large-box model. Constructions and lower bounds show why a naive random-integer model for the discriminant can be misleading.
references.venue: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Galois groups of random integer polynomials and van der Waerden’s Conjecture
references.section: Counting by height and probabilistic Galois theory
references.annotation: Proves the order-of-magnitude bound O(H^(n-1)) for monic integer polynomials of each fixed degree n ≥ 3 and height at most H whose Galois group is not S_n. Degree is fixed; this does not settle the fixed-coefficient-law, growing-degree problem.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Odlyzko, A. M. and Poonen, Bjorn
references.title: Zeros of polynomials with 0,1 coefficients
references.annotation: Poses the asymptotic irreducibility question for monic 0–1 polynomials with constant coefficient 1. Its principal results concern the geometry and topology of their zero sets.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: On the number of irreducible polynomials with 0,1 coefficients
references.annotation: For the 0–1 model, unconditionally excludes small-degree factors with high probability and obtains a lower bound of order 1/log n for irreducibility, using finite-field and exponential-sum methods.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Is a bivariate polynomial with ±1 coefficients irreducible? Very likely!
references.annotation: Studies irreducibility of random bivariate sign polynomials. The additional variable permits arguments unavailable in the univariate fixed-coefficient model.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Borst, Christian and Boyd, Evan and Brekken, Claire and Solberg, Samantha and Wood, Melanie Matchett and Wood, Philip Matchett
references.title: Irreducibility of random polynomials
references.annotation: Computational study of several sampling models and a universality heuristic relating reducibility to low-degree factors. Treat its numerical evidence and conjectures separately from its rigorous statements.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Breuillard, Emmanuel and Varjú, Péter P.
references.title: Irreducibility of random polynomials of large degree
references.annotation: Under Riemann hypotheses for suitable Dedekind zeta functions, proves irreducibility and alternating-group containment for broad independent-coefficient models, with careful treatment of zero and cyclotomic factors. The method connects finite-field random walks, root counts and effective prime-ideal estimates.
references.status: Published; main general results conditional on RH
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: O’Rourke, Sean and Wood, Philip Matchett
references.title: Low-degree factors of random polynomials
references.annotation: Converts pointwise delocalization of roots into exclusion of factors of low algebraic degree. Covers several random-matrix characteristic-polynomial models as well as random polynomials; absence of low-degree factors alone is weaker than irreducibility.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Irreducible polynomials of bounded height
references.annotation: Proves high-probability irreducibility and containment of A_n for suitable fixed coefficient distributions, including uniform coefficients in {1,...,210}. Combines reductions at several primes with probabilistic permutation-group arguments.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Bary-Soroker, Lior and Koukoulopoulos, Dimitris and Kozma, Gady
references.title: Irreducibility of random polynomials: general measures
references.annotation: Develops Fourier equidistribution, a sieve for factor degrees and permutation-group methods for independent integer coefficients, conditioning on nonzero constant term. Proves high-probability irreducibility and Galois group A_n or S_n under explicit distributional hypotheses, including a uniform interval of at least 35 integers; much more general laws yield exclusion of factors up to a positive fraction of the degree.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Full Galois groups of polynomials with slowly growing coefficients
references.annotation: For monic degree-n polynomials with coefficients uniform in [-L(n),L(n)], proves full symmetric Galois group with high probability whenever L(n) tends to infinity. The interval may grow arbitrarily slowly; the theorem does not assert the same conclusion for a fixed interval.
references.venue: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Bary-Soroker, Lior and Hokken, David and Kozma, Gady and Poonen, Bjorn
references.title: Irreducibility of Littlewood polynomials of special degrees
references.annotation: Proves unconditionally that the limsup of the irreducibility probability for uniformly random Littlewood polynomials is 1, using factorization constraints in special degrees. This does not establish an all-degree limit.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Irreducibility of random polynomials of ℤ[X]
references.annotation: Improves rates in the Bary-Soroker–Koukoulopoulos–Kozma framework when near-uniformity holds modulo more primes. The zero-constant-term obstruction remains: for example, uniform intervals of length at least 10^8 give P(reducible) ≤ P(a_0=0)+O(n^(-1/2)), rather than an unconditioned bound tending to zero.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Irreducibility and Galois groups of random reciprocal polynomials of large degree
references.annotation: For reciprocal polynomials of degree 2m and coefficient laws satisfying a Fourier hypothesis, proves high-probability irreducibility and a Galois group equal to the hyperoctahedral group or one of two index-two subgroups. The paired-root symmetry changes both the natural ambient group and the factorization arguments.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Blachar, Guy and Breuillard, Emmanuel and Kozma, Gady
references.title: Galois groups of random polynomials of large degree
references.annotation: Preprint reporting an O(1/log n) square-discriminant probability bound in a high-entropy bounded-coefficient model (Rényi entropy of order 2 greater than 12). The atlas reports the constant-term-one subclass and the uniform-interval full-S_n corollary conditioned on a nonzero constant term. The unqualified v1 statement permits a zero constant term and misses the persistent discriminant-zero event when the first two coefficients vanish; the full proof has not been independently verified.
references.status: Preprint; version 1 dated 30 September 2026; scope issue noted
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.metadata_note: Theorem 1.1 in v1 includes square discriminant without excluding zero and permits an arbitrary independent bounded constant-term law. If the constant and linear coefficients are iid with law μ and μ(0)>0, discriminant zero has probability at least μ(0)^2, contradicting the unrestricted bound. Section 8 invokes an O(1/n) repeated-root bound without removing this event. The website records only the a0=1 reported subclass and the explicitly conditioned interval corollary; it does not certify or repair the preprint proof.

references.title: The Odlyzko-Poonen Conjecture on Irreducibility of Random Polynomials
references.annotation: Preprint presenting an unconditional proof of the irreducibility limit for monic polynomials with constant coefficient 1 and all remaining coefficients independent uniform in {0,1}. The claim concerns this coefficient model and remains a preprint result.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Varjú, Péter P. and Xu, Max Wenqiang
references.title: A random polynomial with multiplicative coefficients is almost surely irreducible
references.annotation: Under RH for Dedekind zeta functions, proves irreducibility with probability 1-O(d^(-1/2+epsilon)) for specified random multiplicative-coefficient models. The theorem concerns P_d(x)/x, after removal of the obligatory factor x; these coefficients are dependent.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Walks on groups, counting reducible matrices, polynomials, and surface and free group automorphisms
references.annotation: Relates random walks on arithmetic groups and finite quotients to irreducible characteristic polynomials. Its random-walk and height models differ from models with independent bounded matrix entries.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: The characteristic polynomial of a random matrix
references.annotation: Assuming ERH, proves high-probability irreducibility and containment of A_n for characteristic polynomials of matrices with independent entries from a fixed nontrivial finitely supported integer law. The dependent polynomial coefficients require matrix-specific input.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Ferber, Asaf and Jain, Vishesh and Sah, Ashwin and Sawhney, Mehtaab
references.title: Random symmetric matrices: rank distribution and irreducibility of the characteristic polynomial
references.annotation: Under ERH, proves high-probability irreducibility for characteristic polynomials of random symmetric sign matrices, using sharp finite-field rank-distribution estimates and inverse Littlewood-Offord methods.
references.status: Published; irreducibility application conditional on ERH
references.venue: Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Anderson, Theresa C. and O’Dorney, Evan M.
references.title: Galois groups of random integer matrices
references.annotation: Studies fixed-size integer matrices with entries bounded by a height parameter and counts characteristic polynomials with non-symmetric Galois group. Uses the large sieve, Fourier analysis and geometric sieving; this is a different asymptotic regime from Eberhard’s growing-dimension theorem.
references.venue: Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Bary-Soroker, Lior and Garzoni, Daniele and Sodin, Sasha
references.title: Irreducibility of the characteristic polynomials of random tridiagonal matrices
references.annotation: Under RH for certain Dedekind zeta functions, proves irreducibility with exponentially high probability and alternating-or-symmetric Galois group for a specified tridiagonal model. A related model has a smaller Galois group.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: On random generation of the symmetric group
references.annotation: Supplies the permutation-group principle behind several probabilistic Galois arguments: a random permutation rarely belongs to a proper transitive subgroup other than A_n. Invariable generation is relevant because modular factorization determines conjugacy classes, rather than labeled permutations.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Eberhard, Sean and Ford, Kevin and Koukoulopoulos, Dimitris
references.title: Permutations contained in transitive subgroups
references.annotation: Sharpens quantitative bounds for permutations lying in transitive subgroups other than S_n or A_n. It treats imprimitive and primitive obstructions separately, supplying estimates for large-group arguments after irreducibility has been established.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.authors: Eberhard, Sean and Ford, Kevin and Green, Ben
references.title: Invariable generation of the symmetric group
references.annotation: Shows that three uniform random permutations fail to invariably generate S_n with probability tending to one, whereas four succeed with probability bounded away from zero. Explains why information from a small fixed collection of modular factorizations has a nontrivial combinatorial threshold.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices

references.title: Ueber die Irreducibilität ganzer rationaler Functionen mit ganzzahligen Coefficienten
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
references.annotation: The original source for Hilbert's irreducibility theorem. It is the historical starting point for passing from irreducible polynomial families over a rational function field to irreducible arithmetic specializations; use a modern treatment for the general language of Hilbertian fields.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.title: Fields containing values of algebraic functions
references.venue: Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, Classe di Scienze (4)
references.annotation: Studies the number fields generated by specialized values of algebraic functions, addressing the diversity of fields obtained from irreducible specializations.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.title: Specializations of one-parameter families of polynomials
references.annotation: Develops geometric and group-theoretic conditions that make the exceptional set of reducible specializations over a number field finite. For fixed n ≥ 10, all but finitely many parameter values in any fixed number field give irreducible generalized Laguerre polynomials with Galois group S_n.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.title: Cyclotomic Diophantine problems (Hilbert irreducibility and invariant sets for polynomial maps)
references.annotation: Develops Hilbert irreducibility in cyclotomic extensions through the arithmetic of torsion points on tori. Applications to roots-of-unity parameters or dynamics over cyclotomic fields require the stated structural hypotheses.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.title: Topics in Galois Theory
references.venue: A K Peters/CRC Press, Research Notes in Mathematics 1
references.annotation: Treats Hilbert irreducibility, thin sets, explicit Galois realizations, rigidity, and sieve methods. Chapter 3 and Section 4.6 explain preservation of generic Galois groups under specialization. Section 4.4 proves the Morse criterion using inertia and Riemann–Hurwitz to obtain full symmetric monodromy.
references.note: Notes written by Henri Darmon. Publisher electronic edition copyright 2007; the physical second edition is also commonly catalogued and cited as 2008.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.title: Hilbert irreducibility above algebraic groups
references.annotation: Studies irreducible fibers above Zariski-dense cyclic subgroups of algebraic tori and powers of an elliptic curve without complex multiplication, under a pullback irreducibility condition. The method combines torsion specialization with descent using Chebotarev, and yields a Bertini-type result for tori.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.title: Specialization results in Galois theory
references.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Uses twisting to turn prescribed specialization questions into rational-point questions. One application combines irreducible specialization with prescribed residue-degree partitions at finitely many sufficiently large primes for covers over Q with geometric monodromy S_n.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.authors: Fried, Michael D. and Jarden, Moshe
references.title: Field Arithmetic
references.venue: Springer, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete, 3. Folge, 11
references.annotation: Treats Hilbertian fields, absolute Galois groups, specialization, and PAC fields. The fourth edition updates the earlier editions and adds a chapter on Hilbertian subfields of Galois extensions.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.title: Groups as Galois Groups: An Introduction
references.section: Generic polynomials and inverse Galois theory
references.annotation: Develops the geometric approach to inverse Galois theory through covers, Riemann’s existence theorem, and rigidity, constructing polynomial families from prescribed permutation data.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.authors: Jensen, Christian U. and Ledet, Arne and Yui, Noriko
references.title: Generic Polynomials: Constructive Aspects of the Inverse Galois Problem
references.section: Generic polynomials and inverse Galois theory
references.annotation: Constructs generic polynomials using invariant-theoretic methods. The MSRI/SLMath page provides free downloadable chapters and explicit families for specified finite groups.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.authors: Malle, Gunter and Matzat, B. Heinrich
references.title: Inverse Galois Theory
references.section: Generic polynomials and inverse Galois theory
references.annotation: A systematic reference for constructing Galois extensions through rigidity, braid actions, embedding problems, additive polynomials, and rigid analytic methods. It also includes tables of example polynomials for transitive and primitive groups of small degree.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.title: The Galois Theory of Iterates and Composites of Polynomials
references.venue: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (3)
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Studies Galois groups under composition and iteration. In characteristic zero, the iterates of the generic degree-d polynomial have the full iterated wreath-product group, giving finite-level specialization results and motivating arboreal questions.

references.title: Galois groups over Q of some iterated polynomials
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Characterizes maximality of iterated quadratic Galois groups through arithmetic square-class conditions, relating critical orbits to the growth of splitting fields.

references.authors: Ayad, Mohamed and McQuillan, Donald L.
references.title: Irreducibility of the iterates of a quadratic polynomial over a field
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Develops criteria for irreducibility of successive quadratic iterates. Read it together with the authors' 2001 correction before using the stated tests in a proof or computation.

references.authors: Ayad, Mohamed and McQuillan, Donald L.
references.title: Corrections to "Irreducibility of the iterates of a quadratic polynomial over a field" (Acta Arith. 93 (2000), 87--97)
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Corrects Ayad and McQuillan’s quadratic-iteration paper and should be read with the original article.

references.title: An iterative construction of irreducible polynomials reducible modulo every prime
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Constructs polynomials of arbitrarily large degree that are irreducible over Q, and over suitable other global fields, but reducible modulo every prime. Failure to find an irreducible reduction is therefore not evidence of reducibility over the ground field.

references.title: Galois representations from pre-image trees: an arboreal survey
references.venue: Publications mathématiques de Besançon. Algèbre et théorie des nombres
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Surveys Galois actions on trees of iterated preimages, stability, and density questions. Its bibliography covers the foundational literature; its open-problem discussion predates subsequent results.

references.title: Polynomials with Surjective Arboreal Galois Representations Exist in Every Degree
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Gives the number-field form of Odoni's existence conjecture in all degrees. The source checked is the 2018 preprint, cited as such in subsequent literature; this must be distinguished from the false assertion over all Hilbertian fields.

references.authors: Benedetto, Robert L. and Juul, Jamie
references.title: Odoni's conjecture for number fields
references.venue: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Proves existence of full arboreal Galois groups for even degree over every number field and for odd degree when the number field has odd degree over Q. The paper does not cover every number-field case suggested by the title.

references.title: Iterates of Generic Polynomials and Generic Rational Functions
references.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Extends the generic full wreath-product result to arbitrary characteristic for rational functions and to polynomials except the degree-2, characteristic-2 case. The paper also records the contributions of Odoni's unpublished work to these results.

references.title: Dynamical Galois groups of trinomials and Odoni's conjecture
references.venue: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Constructs integral polynomials with surjective arboreal representations in every prime degree. It also gives conditional results in certain composite degrees using Vojta's conjecture, so the unconditional and conditional statements should be separated.

references.title: Odoni's conjecture on arboreal Galois representations is false
references.venue: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Disproves Odoni’s conjecture over general Hilbertian fields of characteristic zero. The counterexamples do not contradict positive existence results over number fields.

references.title: Prime and composite polynomials
references.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
references.annotation: The classical source for functional decomposition of complex polynomials into indecomposable components. Here prime means indecomposable under composition, not irreducible under multiplication; read together with the erratum in the same volume, p. 431.

references.title: Primitive monodromy groups of polynomials
references.venue: Recent Developments in the Inverse Galois Problem
references.annotation: Classifies geometric monodromy groups of indecomposable complex polynomials and discusses restrictions for polynomials with rational coefficients. The group is that of f(X)−t over a function field, rather than the splitting-field group of f(X) over the coefficient field.

references.authors: Zieve, Michael E. and Müller, Peter
references.title: On Ritt's polynomial decomposition theorems
references.annotation: Describes all complete decompositions of a complex polynomial, refining Ritt’s theory. Both authors’ publication pages list the work as a preprint; no journal publication is asserted here.

references.title: Jordan–Hölder theorem for imprimitivity systems and maximal decompositions of rational functions
references.venue: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Studies imprimitivity lattices for permutation groups with a cyclic subgroup having at most two orbits, with applications to decomposition. It extends aspects of Ritt's first theorem and explains why unrestricted rational-function analogues can fail.

references.title: New algorithms for finding irreducible polynomials over finite fields
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Constructs irreducible polynomials of a prescribed degree, including deterministic polynomial-time results for small characteristic. Distinguish dependence polynomial in the characteristic from dependence polynomial in its bit length.

references.authors: Hansen, Tom and Mullen, Gary L.
references.title: Primitive polynomials over finite fields
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Provides explicit primitive-polynomial tables and formulates influential existence conjectures with one prescribed coefficient. The primitivity question and the irreducibility question are distinct; a primitive polynomial has a root generating the multiplicative group of the extension field.

references.title: Fast construction of irreducible polynomials over finite fields
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Gives faster algorithms for constructing an irreducible polynomial of specified degree over a finite field, thereby producing an explicit representation of the corresponding extension field.

references.title: Generators and irreducible polynomials over finite fields
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Uses character-sum estimates to study generators and irreducible polynomials with prescribed coefficients. Establishes the Hansen–Mullen irreducibility assertion outside finitely many cases; Ham and Mullen settle the remaining cases.

references.authors: Ham, Kie H. and Mullen, Gary L.
references.title: Distribution of irreducible polynomials of small degrees over finite fields
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Completes the Hansen–Mullen irreducibility conjecture by verifying the finite set of cases left by Wan's theorem. The statement includes necessary exceptions, notably a prescribed zero constant coefficient and the quadratic zero-linear-coefficient case in characteristic two.

references.title: Primitive polynomials with a prescribed coefficient
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Establishes the Hansen–Mullen primitivity assertion for degrees at least nine by character-sum and sieve methods. This is a stronger condition than irreducibility and this paper alone is not the full treatment of the small-degree cases.

references.authors: Mullen, Gary L. and Panario, Daniel
references.editors: Mullen, Gary L. and Panario, Daniel
references.title: Handbook of Finite Fields
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Treats irreducible and primitive polynomials, prescribed coefficients, factorization algorithms, and finite-field applications, with an extensive bibliography.

references.title: Irreducible polynomials with several prescribed coefficients
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Gives an explicit estimate for monic irreducibles with coefficients prescribed at arbitrary positions, with a nonzero constant term when it is prescribed. For sufficiently large degree n, it allows about (1−ε)√n prescribed coefficients uniformly over the ground finite field.

references.title: Irreducible polynomials with several prescribed coefficients
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Improves prescribed-coefficient results to a positive proportion of the degree by adapting Bourgain's method. Its large-field range approaches one quarter of the coefficients; the characteristic, size, and nonzero-constant-term conditions must be retained when applying the theorem.

references.title: A new proof of the Hansen–Mullen irreducibility conjecture
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Proves the one-prescribed-coefficient existence theorem using least periods of discrete Fourier transforms over finite fields. This replaces the character-sum approach while retaining the necessary exceptional cases.

references.title: Factorization of polynomials over finite fields
references.section: Finite fields: factorization statistics and monodromy
references.annotation: Presents the Stickelberger discriminant-parity theorem, including characteristic two via lifting, and derives reducibility obstructions for binary trinomials. Swan explicitly credits the basic parity theorem to Stickelberger and notes Dalen's earlier proof.

references.title: The distribution of polynomials over finite fields
references.section: Finite fields: factorization statistics and monodromy
references.annotation: Studies factorization patterns of f(X)-a g(X) as a varies over a finite field, relating factor degrees to cycle types in a function-field Galois group under the stated arithmetic hypotheses.

references.authors: Guralnick, Robert M. and Zieve, Michael E.
references.title: Polynomials with PSL(2) monodromy
references.section: Finite fields: factorization statistics and monodromy
references.annotation: Classifies positive-characteristic polynomials with specified PSL(2) monodromy under a ramification hypothesis, with applications to exceptional polynomials and decomposition after extending constants. This concerns function-field Galois groups; splitting fields of individual polynomials over finite fields have cyclic Galois groups.

references.authors: Bank, Efrat and Bary-Soroker, Lior and Rosenzweig, Lior
references.title: Prime polynomials in short intervals and in arithmetic progressions
references.section: Finite fields: factorization statistics and monodromy
references.annotation: Proves asymptotic counts for irreducibles in short polynomial intervals and arithmetic progressions, and treats other factorization types. The asymptotic is fixed degree with the field size tending to infinity, with explicit small-characteristic and interval-length restrictions.

references.title: Factorization statistics of restricted polynomial specializations over large finite fields
references.section: Finite fields: factorization statistics and monodromy
references.annotation: Studies factorization patterns when specialization parameters are restricted to sufficiently large, regular subsets of a prime field. The degree stays fixed as the characteristic tends to infinity; the result is not a growing-degree statement over one fixed finite field.

references.title: Factoring polynomials over finite fields
references.annotation: Factors polynomials over finite fields by linear algebra in the Frobenius-fixed subalgebra, which detects the irreducible factors.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: On Hensel factorization, I
references.annotation: The classical modular route to integer-polynomial factorization: factor modulo a prime, lift p-adically, then recombine the lifted factors. It explains why local factors must be grouped before recovering rational factors.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Probabilistic algorithms in finite fields
references.annotation: Develops finite-field algorithms for irreducible-polynomial construction, root finding, and factorization, alongside Frobenius-power tests for irreducibility of monic polynomials.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups
references.metadata_note: The MIT repository link describes the earlier January 1979 report Probabilistic Algorithm in Finite Fields (MIT-LCS-TR-213). This entry cites the 1980 SIAM journal article; the repository report and journal version have different publication dates.

references.authors: Cantor, David G. and Zassenhaus, Hans
references.title: A new algorithm for factoring polynomials over finite fields
references.annotation: Gives a randomized finite-field factorization algorithm, including the splitting of products whose irreducible factors have equal degree. The search is randomized; the resulting factors can be checked exactly.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.authors: Lenstra, A. K. and Lenstra, Jr., H. W. and Lovász, L.
references.title: Factoring polynomials with rational coefficients
references.annotation: Proves polynomial-time factorization over the rationals using lattice basis reduction. The lattice algorithm also supports algebraic-relation searches and certificate construction.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups
references.metadata_note: The CWI record is the 1982 preprint report IW 195/82; the UC Davis link supplies scanned full text. The Numdam link is the 2009 Belabas–van Hoeij–Klüners–Steel follow-up, not another edition of this 1982 article.

references.title: A new polynomial factorization algorithm and its implementation
references.annotation: Develops and implements baby-step/giant-step finite-field factorization, examining its computational performance.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups
references.metadata_note: The open-text link is the author's version. The published article appeared in Journal of Symbolic Computation 20(4), October 1995, pages 363–397.

references.title: Subquadratic-time factoring of polynomials over finite fields
references.annotation: Improves the complexity of randomized polynomial factorization over finite fields through a baby-step/giant-step framework used in later factorization algorithms.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups
references.metadata_note: The open-text link is the authors' version of the journal work. The 1998 Mathematics of Computation article expands an extended abstract presented at STOC 1995; the two publication dates identify different versions.

references.title: Factoring polynomials and the knapsack problem
references.annotation: Replaces the recombination search in modular factorization with a structured knapsack problem solved by lattice reduction.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups
references.metadata_note: The open-text link is the author's version. The journal publication is August 2002; the year 2001 embedded in its DOI is not the publication year.

references.authors: Belabas, Karim and van Hoeij, Mark and Klüners, Jürgen and Steel, Allan
references.title: Factoring polynomials over global fields
references.venue: Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux
references.annotation: Establishes polynomial-time complexity for van Hoeij's original rational factorization algorithm and natural variants. It also treats global-field extensions of the approach and bivariate factorization over finite fields.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: The determination of Galois groups
references.annotation: Introduces subgroup descent using relative invariants and resolvents, a method underlying later Galois-group algorithms.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.authors: Landau, Susan and Miller, Gary Lee
references.title: Solvability by radicals is in polynomial time
references.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
references.annotation: Shows that deciding solvability by radicals for rational polynomials is possible in polynomial time. This decision problem should be distinguished from constructing an entire splitting field or listing every element of a large Galois group.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Computing Galois groups over the rationals
references.annotation: Develops practical computational methods using resolvents and low-degree transitive groups. The paper also gives rational realizations of the transitive permutation groups in degrees three through seven.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Solving solvable quintics
references.annotation: A concrete sextic-resolvent treatment of solvable irreducible quintics and radical expressions. Use it with Robin Chapman's 1992 correction to the proof of Theorem 1 and the numerical errata on the author's webpage.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Galois group computation for rational polynomials
references.annotation: Develops Galois-group computation using p-adic roots and refinements of Stauduhar’s method, preceding Fieker and Klüners’s approach without an a priori degree bound.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Explicit Galois realization of transitive groups of degree up to 15
references.annotation: Constructs explicit rational polynomials realizing all transitive groups of degree at most fifteen and organizes the constructions by permutation group.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Identifying Frobenius elements in Galois groups
references.annotation: Identifies Frobenius conjugacy classes beyond the factor-degree data of reduction modulo a prime, distinguishing classes that share a cycle type in the chosen permutation representation.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Computation of Galois groups of rational polynomials
references.venue: LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics
references.annotation: Constructs relative invariants for Galois-group computation without an a priori degree bound. The method underlies current Magma computations, subject to practical time and memory limits.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory
references.annotation: Develops algorithms for polynomial factorization, number fields, and Galois-group computation, with the arithmetic needed for their implementation.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.authors: von zur Gathen, Joachim and Gerhard, Jürgen
references.title: Modern Computer Algebra
references.annotation: Treats polynomial arithmetic, finite-field factorization, Hensel lifting, and factorization over the rationals, with complexity models and algorithmic proofs.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: A database for field extensions of the rationals
references.venue: LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics
references.annotation: Explains the arithmetic database, its construction methods, and its emphasis on Galois groups and signatures. Consult the live database separately, since its coverage has grown beyond the original paper.

references.title: FLINT documentation: polynomial factorization algorithms
references.annotation: Official explanations of finite-field and integer-polynomial factorization, connecting Berlekamp, Cantor–Zassenhaus, Hensel lifting, and lattice recombination with library routines. These are implementation guides; use the cited original papers for theorem statements and complexity proofs.
references.status: Maintained software documentation; revision in progress
references.metadata_note: The documentation was undergoing a major revision when checked. Its October 2026 banner states that parts of the text were generated by an LLM and asks readers to report inaccuracies. Mathematical claims in this atlas are independently supported by the original research papers.

references.title: A database for number fields
references.annotation: A source of defining polynomials indexed by Galois group and signature. At access, the site reports coverage through degree twenty-three for all transitive groups except M23, with stated limitations on signatures and discriminant minima.

references.title: The L-functions and Modular Forms Database: number fields and Galois groups
references.annotation: Searchable number-field records and transitive-group data, with labels, invariants, and links between objects. Consult the completeness and reliability pages for each collection; a group appearing in a transitive-group catalogue does not by itself prove its realization over the rationals.
references.metadata_note: Number-field completeness is bounded by degree, signature, discriminant, or ramification conditions. The reliability page marks certain class-group and unit data that depend on GRH. Transitive-group catalogue completeness is a separate statement and does not establish realization over the rationals.

references.title: Magma Handbook: Galois groups
references.annotation: Official documentation for the Stauduhar-based GaloisGroup implementation, with no fixed degree cap for the documented integer, rational and number-field polynomial inputs. GaloisGroup does not itself certify its conditional steps; the documented GaloisProof overloads attempt certification for integer polynomials or absolute number fields. Record a successful result and the exact input/options.

references.title: PARI/GP reference manual: general number fields and polgalois
references.annotation: Official reference for polgalois and number-field computations. PARI/GP 2.19 requires irreducible rational input of degree at most seven, or eleven with galdata. The manual explicitly warns that insufficient initial precision can rarely produce a wrong result; record precision, output convention, and version.

references.title: SageMath reference manual: polynomial and number-field Galois groups
references.annotation: Official interfaces for polynomial and number-field Galois groups. SageMath 10.10 documents PARI through degree 11, GAP fallback with a documented range through degree 15 and some higher examples, and a Magma wrapper limited by group identification through degree 30. The number-field interface distinguishes original-root and Galois-closure actions and warns about absolute versus relative ground fields. A wrapper is not an independent backend proof.

references.title: Reduzibilität ebener Kurven
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik
references.annotation: A classical source on reducibility of plane curves and algebraic criteria for absolute irreducibility. This is a multivariate question: a univariate polynomial of degree greater than one always splits over an algebraic closure.
references.metadata_note: Bibliographic details checked in Lecerf's survey and an AMS bibliography; the publisher full text was not retrieved.
