references.title: Effective Noether irreducibility forms and applications
references.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
references.annotation: Gives effective bounds for algebraic irreducibility criteria, with applications to exceptional specializations in several variables and to factorization complexity.

references.title: Absolute irreducibility of polynomials via Newton polytopes
references.annotation: Uses integral indecomposability of Newton polytopes to obtain absolute irreducibility criteria for sparse multivariate polynomials. Monomial factors must be excluded when applying a polytope criterion to a polynomial.

references.title: Factoring multivariate polynomials via partial differential equations
references.annotation: A factorization method based on a differential equation and linear algebra, in characteristic zero or sufficiently large characteristic. Connects rational and absolute factorization and provides an effective reduction from multivariate to bivariate problems.

references.title: Factorisation des polynômes à plusieurs variables
references.venue: Journées Nationales de Calcul Formel (13–17 May 2013)
references.annotation: A French-language course on multivariate factorization, including absolute factorization and computational algebraic geometry, with an extensive bibliography.
references.note: Journées Nationales de Calcul Formel, 13–17 May 2013, talk 2.

references.title: Math 788F: The Theory of Irreducible Polynomials
references.venue: University of South Carolina course materials
references.annotation: Provides a syllabus, problems, and an introduction to Newton polygons for a course on irreducibility methods. The page does not currently link openly to every chapter of the proposed book.

references.title: An irreducible that factors modulo all primes
references.annotation: Explains why irreducibility over the rationals need not be detectable by one irreducible reduction. The obstruction is visible in the cycle types available in the Galois group.

references.title: Galois groups of cubics and quartics (not in characteristic 2)
references.annotation: Worked low-degree classifications using discriminants and resolvents. The characteristic restriction matters; the author’s collection also contains a separate all-characteristics treatment.

references.title: Irreducibility tests in F_p[T]
references.annotation: Explains finite-field irreducibility tests and the congruence and gcd calculations that give modular certificates.

references.title: Irreducibility tests in Q[T]
references.annotation: Proves Gauss’s lemma, the reduction-modulo-a-prime criterion, and Eisenstein’s criterion, establishing the prerequisites for more specialized irreducibility tests.

references.title: Galois groups over Q and factorizations mod p
references.annotation: Explains how squarefree factorizations modulo good primes produce cycle types in a Galois group, with an explicit discriminant condition.

references.title: Recognizing Galois groups S_n and A_n
references.annotation: Gives permutation-group recognition criteria and examples that use modular factorization and real roots to identify S_n or A_n.

references.title: Hilbert’s Irreducibility for $\mathbb{G}_m$
references.annotation: Describes exceptional S-unit fibers of a curve cover as a finite set together with finitely many power cosets. Theorem 3 makes the cosets effective but leaves the finite remainder ineffective; Corollary 1 characterizes infinitely many reducible f(x)−p_1^{e_1}⋯p_s^{e_s}.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory
references.metadata_note: Source title uses the notation G_m for the multiplicative group; author order in the PDF is Samir Siksek and Michael Stoll.

references.title: When do all iterates of x²+a have maximal Galois group?
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Reworks quadratic critical-orbit criteria and extends explicit sufficient conditions to rational parameters. Theorem 6.1 imposes region and congruence restrictions; Conjecture 8.1 asks for uniform finite-level detection. Neither the computational evidence nor the reported formalization establishes that conjecture in general.

references.authors: Gao, Shuhong and Lauder, Alan G. B.
references.title: Decomposition of Polytopes and Polynomials
references.annotation: Relates Minkowski decompositions of lattice polytopes to possible polynomial factors, gives polygon-decomposition algorithms, and develops projection tests in higher dimension. Corollary 2 gives an absolute-irreducibility certificate with the necessary exclusion of monomial factors. A decomposable polytope is inconclusive.

references.authors: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
references.title: Bernoulli and Euler Polynomials (Chapter 24)
references.venue: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials
references.annotation: Gives conventions, generating identities, Bernoulli denominator arithmetic, and complete multiple-root classifications: every B_n is squarefree; E_5 is the unique Euler exception. Appell Euler polynomials are distinct from Eulerian descent polynomials.

references.title: A proof of the irreducibility conjecture for Legendre polynomials
references.section: Special families: Jacobi, Legendre and related polynomials
references.annotation: Preprint claiming a proof of Stieltjes’ irreducibility conjecture for parity-normalized Legendre polynomials in every degree, using upper and lower bounds for a resultant. Included to keep the historical conjecture record current; the full proof has not been independently verified in this atlas.
references.status: Preprint claim; version 2, 27 September 2026; no peer-reviewed publication verified

references.title: On the factorization of Eulerian polynomials
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials
references.annotation: Studies arithmetic factorization of Eulerian polynomials, including the lower bound p−1 for the degree of a large irreducible factor when p is the largest prime not exceeding the index. The atlas gives an elementary Newton-polygon derivation and the prime-plus-one consequence.
references.status: Published article; original full text not accessed in this review
references.metadata_note: Publication metadata cross-checked in the University of Utah journal bibliography; the factor-degree result is attributed to Heidrich in the introduction of Ta Thi Hoai An and Ngo Quoc Hoan, Multiple Eulerian polynomials. No original-paper theorem number is claimed.

references.authors: Chidambaram, Shiva and Mináč, Ján and Nguyen, Tung T. and Tân, Nguyen Duy
references.title: Fekete polynomials of principal Dirichlet characters
references.section: Special families: Fekete and reciprocal polynomials
references.annotation: Studies the 0/1 polynomials associated with principal Dirichlet characters: cyclotomic factors, the remaining polynomial, separability, and Galois groups. Distinct from the prime-conductor quadratic-character family; records conjectures suggested by calculations.
references.metadata_note: Use publisher year2025, volume1(1), pp51–93. Some discovery indexes display2026, but the journal page and PDF state2025.

references.title: On multiple zeros of Bernoulli polynomials
references.annotation: Completes the proof that every Bernoulli polynomial is squarefree, using Brillhart’s restriction on possible multiple roots and congruences for centered expansions. Section 4 recalls that E_5 is the unique Euler polynomial with multiple roots.
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials

references.title: On universal higher order Bernoulli numbers and polynomials
references.venue: Report of the Research Institute of Industrial Technology, Nihon University
references.annotation: Research report on Bernoulli families and generalizations. Section 2 states Carlitz’s even-index irreducibility criterion and its relation to McCarthy’s base-p digit-sum condition; later sections discuss higher-order and universal versions.
references.metadata_note: Report number 70 (2003), ISSN 0386-1678. The report’s definition of p-Eisenstein indexes coefficients in descending order; the atlas uses the equivalent usual Eisenstein criterion on the reciprocal polynomial.
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials

references.title: On powers that are sums of consecutive like powers
references.annotation: Proves an unconditional derangement theorem for even Bernoulli Galois groups, using 2-adic Newton polygons and decomposition groups. Applies Chebotarev to equations involving sums of powers; records the even-index irreducibility conjecture.
references.section: Special families: Euler, Bernoulli and Eulerian polynomials

references.title: Algebraic Number Theory (v3.08)
references.annotation: Free notes supplying precise proofs of the discriminant–index identity, prime decomposition, Hensel lifting, unramified extensions, decomposition groups, and tame/wild inertia. Version 3.08 is dated 19 July 2020; this is a different work from Fields and Galois Theory.

references.title: Galois groups of twisted reciprocal polynomials: a uniform asymptotic
references.section: Special families: Fekete and reciprocal polynomials
references.annotation: For fixed twist b≠0 and half-degree m≥4, reports an asymptotic for exceptional hyperoctahedral Galois groups in an adapted Euclidean height. Primary arXiv indexed abstract checked; theorem details and constants require the full version.
references.metadata_note: The primary arXiv abstract and v1 endpoint could not be reopened on 12 November 2026. The earlier abstract-only catalogue entry is retained; full theorem statements, constants and any later version remain unverified in this pass.

references.authors: Guàrdia, Jordi and Montes, Jesús and Nart, Enric
references.title: Newton polygons of higher order in algebraic number theory
references.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Develops Ore’s higher Newton polygons for local factorization. Product and residual-polynomial theorems refine slope restrictions to irreducibility certificates, and higher-order indices control termination. These methods address repeated factors in reduction and cases where a first Newton polygon is inconclusive. Theorem numbers cited in this atlas refer to arXiv v2 where indicated.
references.status: Published article; open author preprint v2 (2008)
references.section: Local irreducibility and higher Newton polygons

references.authors: Guàrdia, Jordi and Montes, Jesús and Nart, Enric
references.title: Higher Newton polygons in the computation of discriminants and prime ideal decomposition in number fields
references.venue: Journal de théorie des nombres de Bordeaux
references.annotation: Presents an optimized Montes method using types and their representatives. Complete types identify irreducible local factors and reveal ramification indices and residue degrees; the algorithm computes prime ideal decomposition and local index information without requiring a global integral basis first.
references.section: Algorithms for local factorization and number fields
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Local Polynomial Factorisation: Improving the Montes Algorithm
references.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 International Symposium on Symbolic and Algebraic Computation (ISSAC ’22)
references.annotation: Improves local irreducibility and factorization using generalized Hensel lifting, approximate roots, and divide-and-conquer. The sharper complexity bounds require residue characteristic zero or sufficiently large; the source separately includes residual-field factorization costs. A same-title arXiv record, 2607.02153 (2 July 2026), is linked as a related deposit, not a separate discovery; its full text could not be retrieved in this audit.
references.status: Published conference paper (5 July 2022); related 2026 arXiv deposit
references.section: Algorithms for local factorization and number fields
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: An Elementary Test for the Galois Group of a Quartic Polynomial
references.annotation: Original source of the elementary quartic-group test that separates cyclic and dihedral cases after the cubic resolvent and discriminant tests. Publisher metadata verified; the full formulation and proof used in this atlas are checked in Conrad’s author-hosted exposition, Theorem 4.1. The publisher also assigns DOI 10.1080/00029890.1989.11972158.
references.group: Galois group detection and effective prime methods

references.authors: Brent, Richard P. and Kung, Hsiang-Tsung
references.title: Fast algorithms for manipulating formal power series
references.annotation: Classical fast composition and reversion algorithms. The baby-step/giant-step matrix method also underlies modular composition; distinguish the arbitrary-modulus version from techniques that use the special modulus x^n. The author page records an erratum on page 590.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.authors: Kedlaya, Kiran S. and Umans, Christopher
references.title: Fast polynomial factorization and modular composition
references.annotation: Proves a near-linear bit-complexity bound for modular composition over finite fields, yielding the degree-3/2 randomized factorization benchmark. The method uses multivariate evaluation and supports fast Frobenius iteration; its bit-complexity bounds differ from field-operation bounds. Corollary 7.2 states the modular-composition bound for each fixed positive epsilon.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.authors: Guo, Zeyu and Narayanan, Anand Kumar and Umans, Chris
references.title: Algebraic problems equivalent to beating exponent 3/2 for polynomial factorization over finite fields
references.annotation: Relates finite-field factorization to other algebraic problems by reductions, identifying improvements that would lower its degree exponent below 3/2. These equivalences do not establish optimality of the exponent 3/2.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups
references.venue: 41st International Symposium on Mathematical Foundations of Computer Science (MFCS 2016), LIPIcs

references.authors: Neiger, Vincent and Salvy, Bruno and Schost, Éric and Villard, Gilles
references.title: Faster modular composition
references.annotation: A Las Vegas algorithm for modular composition over arbitrary fields of known characteristic, with expected arithmetic complexity O(n^1.43). Polynomial matrices encode algebraic relations. Theorem 1.1 detects failed trials; the discussion handles small finite fields by extension. This counts field operations, unlike finite-field bit-complexity bounds.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.authors: Neiger, Vincent and Salvy, Bruno and Schost, Éric and Villard, Gilles
references.title: Faster modular composition using two relation matrices
references.annotation: Theorem 1.3 improves algebraic modular composition to soft-O(n^((omega+3)/4)) for generic inner polynomials relative to a fixed modulus. Genericity failure is detected; an arbitrary-input Las Vegas reduction is left as a research question. Published at ISSAC 2026, with the published version on arXiv v2.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups
references.venue: Proceedings of the 51st International Symposium on Symbolic and Algebraic Computation (ISSAC 2026)

references.authors: van der Hoeven, Joris and Lecerf, Grégoire
references.title: Fast modular composition using spiroids
references.annotation: Gives a sharper nearly linear bit bound for modular composition over Z/rZ using structured complex evaluation points and controlled-precision Fourier transforms. Prime finite fields are included. The authors distinguish asymptotic improvement from practical competitiveness. Journal publication is October 2026.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: A number-theoretic conjecture implying faster algorithms for polynomial factorization and integer factorization
references.annotation: Proposes a structured divisibility-covering conjecture which, under the paper’s hypotheses, would improve the degree exponent for finite-field factorization below 3/2. The improvement is conditional. The work is available as a 2025 preprint and was listed in the December 2026 ISAAC program at the verification date.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Computing the Galois group of a polynomial over a p-adic field
references.annotation: Develops local Galois-group algorithms using resolvents, ramification, and global models; a local group occurs as a decomposition subgroup in a global computation. Remark 3.5 records a heuristic precision bound in the original implementation. The linked package separately documents an exact p-adic input mode for proved results.
references.group: Algorithms for factorization and Galois groups

references.title: Irreducible polynomials over a finite field with restricted coefficients
references.annotation: Counts monic irreducibles when every nonleading coefficient avoids a common small forbidden set. Theorem 1 gives explicit q,n,|R| conditions and a constant-term correction; Theorem 2 uses additional interval structure. The field-size and degree ranges matter.

references.title: Counting irreducible polynomials with restricted coefficients
references.annotation: Extends the common-forbidden-set model to position-dependent forbidden sets. Theorem 1.1 allows at most √q/2 exclusions per coefficient for q≥300 and sufficiently large degree; Corollary 1.3 treats avoiding one specified value at every position. Includes the necessary constant-term density factor.
references.metadata_note: Issue date December 2025. The publisher-indexed article preview supplies Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.3; direct page fetching intermittently returns HTTP 403.

references.title: Irreducibility of polynomials with square coefficients over finite fields
references.annotation: For fixed degree n, independent nonleading coefficients uniform on the set of square values give irreducibility probability 1/n+O_n(q^(−1/2)) as q grows. Theorem 2 covers more general sets of bounded algebraic complexity. Uniform square values differ from squaring uniform field elements in odd characteristic.
references.metadata_note: Published January 2026; DOI contains 2025. Mathematical theorem locators refer to the public author preprint v1, while publication metadata is verified from the author institution and publisher.

references.authors: Bary-Soroker, Lior and Garzoni, Daniele and Matei, Vlad
references.title: On the irreducibility of f(2^n,3^m,X) and other such polynomials
references.section: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory
references.annotation: Under GRH and the geometric pullback condition (PB), Theorem 1.1 proves density-one irreducibility along independent power parameters. The power-pullback condition is stronger than generic irreducibility and excludes X²−t. Theorem 1.1 counts exponent vectors in symmetric boxes, including negative exponents.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory

references.authors: Benedetto, Robert L. and Ghioca, Dragos and Juul, Jamie and Tucker, Thomas J.
references.title: Arboreal Galois groups of postcritically finite quadratic polynomials: The periodic case
references.venue: Journal of the London Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Describes groups for x²+c with periodic critical point in characteristic different from two. Theorem 1.5 gives equivalent square-root, finite-level, and all-level conditions for attaining the specified constrained group, which is not the full binary-tree automorphism group. The target point and cyclotomic constants enter the hypotheses.

references.authors: Benedetto, Robert L. and Ghioca, Dragos and Juul, Jamie and Tucker, Thomas J.
references.title: Arboreal Galois groups of postcritically finite quadratic polynomials: The strictly preperiodic case
references.annotation: Complements the periodic case by treating strictly preperiodic critical orbits of x²+c. Separates short-tail and long-tail cases and gives criteria for the resulting constrained groups. Section 1.4 excludes the already-classical Chebyshev map x²−2, whose towers admit a Kummer description.
references.metadata_note: Published online 30 March 2026; no unverified final volume or page range assigned. Mathematical locators refer to author preprint v1.

references.authors: Laishram, Shanta and Shorey, Tarlok N.
references.title: Irreducibility of generalized Hermite–Laguerre polynomials III
references.annotation: All-degree irreducibility for eight third- and quarter-integer Laguerre parameters, with (q,n)=(1/4,2) exceptional. Only the ordinary assertion is used: the printed power-substitution wording needs qualification because L_1^(-3/4)(x⁴)=1/4−x⁴ is reducible.

references.title: The irreducibility of some Wronskian Hermite polynomials
references.annotation: Studies arithmetic and zeros of two-part Wronskian Hermite families using Newton polygons and Schur congruences. The atlas’s restatement of Theorem 2 excludes the unit remainder R_(2,1)=1, since irreducibility here requires a nonconstant polynomial.

references.title: Classifying families of orthogonal polynomials having Galois group the alternating group
references.annotation: Extends the classification program from square discriminants to alternating Galois groups of generalized Laguerre polynomials, for integer α≠n, up to finitely many exceptions. The diagonal α=n remains outside the stated scope.

references.title: Distribution of the roots of Eulerian polynomials
references.venue: Electronic Communications in Probability (accepted on author page); author manuscript arXiv:2507.15908v2
references.annotation: A combinatorial proof of the known log-Cauchy zero distribution, using moments that become exactly constant. The paper uses x times the Eulerian polynomial normalized here. The author records acceptance; final journal metadata was not independently retrieved.

references.title: Elementary characterization of the Galois groups of x^12+ax^6+b
references.annotation: Classifies the 16 possible groups under irreducibility over Q. Lower-degree power compositions, square and cube tests, and a cubic resolvent give an explicit decision algorithm. Published online 2 September 2026.

references.authors: Awtrey, Chad and Patane, Frank and Toone, Brian
references.title: On Galois groups of power compositional nonic polynomials
references.venue: Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Classifies the 11 possible transitive groups for irreducible g(x³), with g a rational monic cubic, using two discriminants and two resolvents. Also gives an algorithm to recognize number fields with such a defining polynomial. Online 10 February 2025; issue dated December 2025.

references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.authors: Peled, Ron and Sen, Arnab and Zeitouni, Ofer
references.title: Double roots of random Littlewood polynomials
references.annotation: Gives sharp parity-sensitive double-root asymptotics for fair-sign Littlewood polynomials. Separates the easier squarefreeness question from irreducibility and explains the dominant repeated roots at ±1.
references.metadata_note: Theorem 1.2, specialized to fair signs; publication metadata confirmed by the publisher, arXiv and the author’s institutional record. Publisher and institutional abstract rendering interchanges formulas, so mathematical statements were checked against the full paper.

references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.authors: Feldheim, Ohad N. and Sen, Arnab
references.title: Double roots of random polynomials with integer coefficients
references.annotation: For bounded iid integer coefficients with largest atom at most 1/2, locates repeated-root probability at 0 and ±1 up to o(n^(-2)); when zero is excluded, obtains O(n^(-2)). Allowing zero coefficients can leave a persistent discriminant-zero event.
references.metadata_note: Theorem 1.1. The model randomizes every coefficient, including the leading one; it is not stated as a fixed-monic theorem.

references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.title: On the distribution of reducible polynomials
references.section: Counting by height and probabilistic Galois theory
references.annotation: Establishes sharp orders for reducible, not necessarily monic integer polynomials of fixed degree and bounded coefficient height: H^n in degree n≥3, and H^2 log H in degree two. Complements monic counting theorems and isolates the contribution of linear factors.
references.metadata_note: Published in 2009; the author’s arXiv copy was deposited in 2020. Theorems 1–4 in that copy.

references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.title: Counting Polynomials via Galois Actions on Root Subsets
references.section: Counting by height and prescribed permutation actions
references.annotation: Obtains upper bounds for monic bounded-height polynomials with specified permutation representations, including actions on subsets, ordered tuples, and regular actions. The method recovers splitting fields from carefully chosen root-subset stabilizers and controls heights of their generators.
references.metadata_note: Theorems 1.1–1.4; Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 3.3 explain the root-subset mechanism. The HTML title page displays 24 August 2026 although the arXiv record lists only v1 submitted 15 March 2026; version identifier is retained explicitly.

references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.title: Probabilistic Galois theory in function fields
references.status: Published; earlier conditional full-group result superseded in odd characteristic
references.annotation: Studies monic polynomials in y with independent uniformly bounded-degree coefficients in F_q[x]. The two limiting regimes differ: growing coefficient degree gives S_n with probability tending to one; growing y-degree gives irreducibility limit 1−q^(−d), and conditioned on irreducibility, the group is A_n or S_n with probability tending to one. The full-S_n refinement in odd characteristic uses a uniform polynomial Chowla conjecture. Entin’s later 2025 theorem removes the Chowla assumption when q is odd.
references.metadata_note: Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6 checked in arXiv v3 (4 July 2024); the precise uniformity required for the conditional result is Conjecture 1.5. The publisher article endpoint could not be reopened during the 12 November 2026 second pass; publication metadata was retained from the earlier primary-publisher check.

references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.title: Law of large numbers for the discriminant of random polynomials
references.annotation: Proves a universal first-order law for log absolute discriminant of iid mean-zero, variance-one sub-Gaussian Kac polynomials with no zero coefficient atom. Connects Mahler measure, reciprocal symmetry in distribution and root separation. A size asymptotic does not determine the discriminant’s square class.
references.metadata_note: Theorem 1, equation (10), and §1.3. The abstract omits hypotheses that are explicit in Theorem 1; the atlas preserves them.

references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.title: Limit law for root separation in random polynomials
references.annotation: Establishes a limiting law for the smallest root separation at scale n^(-5/4) for mean-zero sub-Gaussian iid coefficients with no atom at zero. Corollary 1.2 implies squarefreeness with probability tending to one without the older integer-law largest-atom restriction.
references.metadata_note: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2; published in June 2026. The sharp Littlewood repeated-root asymptotic of Peled–Sen–Zeitouni supplies a quantitative conclusion not contained in the limit statement alone.

references.title: On the irreducibility of the polynomials P(t^m, Y)
references.annotation: Characterizes infinite reducibility along a geometric progression by a reducible scaled power pullback (Theorem 1.2). Under the geometric pullback condition (PB), one obtains irreducibility for all but finitely many integer exponents, unconditionally. The argument uses Siegel’s theorem; finiteness is distinct from effective enumeration of exceptional exponents.
references.group: Hilbert irreducibility and inverse Galois theory
references.metadata_note: Original scanned author-hosted paper inspected visually: Theorem 1.2 is on printed page 144. Publication metadata verified against the publisher and author list.

references.title: Arithmetic of certain hypergeometric modular forms
references.annotation: Formulates the irreducibility and full-symmetric-group conjecture for Kaneko–Zagier polynomials and proves infinitely many irreducibility cases. The introduction also records the distinct conjecture for Eisenstein-series divisor polynomials.

references.authors: Jindal, Ankita and Nair, Saranya G. and Shorey, Tarlok N.
references.title: Extension of irreducibility results on generalized Laguerre polynomials L_n^(-n-s-1)(x)
references.annotation: Extends irreducibility in the negative-integral two-parameter Laguerre family through s=92. For 93≤s≤100 excludes proper linear factors, and establishes alternating or symmetric groups conditional on irreducibility. The publisher’s abstract was checked; full text was not accessed.

references.authors: Felder, Giovanni and Hemery, Adrian D. and Veselov, Alexander P.
references.title: Zeros of Wronskians of Hermite polynomials and Young diagrams
references.annotation: Relates Hermite-Wronskian zero patterns to partitions and monodromy-free Schrödinger operators. Section 6 states Veselov’s conjecture that every nonzero zero is simple; the origin is explicitly exempt.

references.title: Arithmetic of Jacobi polynomials
references.annotation: Version 1 claims complete proofs of the Mahlburg–Ono conjecture for four Kaneko–Zagier families and of the Cullinan–Hajir Legendre Galois-group conjecture. Included as a dated claim; neither the full proof nor peer-reviewed publication was independently verified here.
references.status: Preprint claim; version 1, 22 October 2026; no peer-reviewed publication verified

references.title: Uniform irreducibility and Galois groups of generalized Laguerre polynomials
references.annotation: Claims a uniform eventual irreducibility and alternating-containment theorem for negative-integral Laguerre parameters, with an effective finite exceptional set. This is not an all-pair resolution of Hajir’s conjectures. The full proof has not been independently verified here.
references.status: Preprint claim; version 1, 4 November 2026; no peer-reviewed publication verified

references.title: On the Newton polygons of Kaneko–Zagier lifts of supersingular polynomials
references.annotation: Computes Newton polygons of four rational supersingular-lift families. Their one-edge cases give further irreducibility results toward the Mahlburg–Ono conjecture.

references.title: An irreducibility question concerning modifications of Laguerre polynomials
references.annotation: Addresses Hajir’s admissible-modification question. For fixed nonnegative r, gives an effective degree bound beyond which every allowed modification is irreducible; also classifies the possible linear-factor exceptions for r≤3.
references.note: Published online 13 December 2019; volume year 2020. Abstract checked in publisher-provided preview.

references.authors: Shorey, Tarlok N. and Sinha, Sneh Bala
references.title: Extension of Laguerre polynomials with negative arguments
references.annotation: Studies arbitrary integral coefficient modifications with endpoint multipliers ±1. Proves restrictions on factor degrees and describes ranges where the polynomial is irreducible or a linear factor times an irreducible polynomial, with explicit exceptional possibilities.

references.authors: Shorey, Tarlok N. and Sinha, Sneh Bala
references.title: Extension of Laguerre polynomials with negative arguments II
references.annotation: Makes the exceptional-pair analysis for admissible modifications explicit through parameter s≤30, building on the preceding paper. The statements concern modified polynomials and must be distinguished from irreducibility of the unmodified Laguerre polynomial.

references.authors: De Angelis, Valerio and Marcello, Dominic
references.title: Wilf’s conjecture
references.annotation: Gives a corrected account of the 2-adic argument showing that at most one index other than 2 can have vanishing complementary Bell number. This concerns rational roots of Touchard polynomials, not their full irreducibility.

references.authors: Amdeberhan, Tewodros and De Angelis, Valerio and Moll, Victor H.
references.title: Complementary Bell Numbers: Arithmetical Properties and Wilf’s Conjecture
references.annotation: Develops valuation methods for complementary Bell numbers and states Wilf’s nonvanishing problem. Read with De Angelis–Marcello (2016), which corrects errors in the earlier proof.

references.authors: Cameron, Peter J. and Morgan, Kerri
references.title: Algebraic properties of chromatic roots
references.annotation: States the α+n and nα conjectures, a conjecture about the nonlinear factor of a random graph’s chromatic polynomial, and the problem of characterizing graphs whose chromatic polynomial splits over Q.

references.title: Chromatic roots as algebraic integers
references.annotation: Proves the α+n conjecture for quadratic and cubic algebraic integers and gives a dense set of chromatic roots satisfying the nα conjecture.
references.metadata_note: The PDF is explicitly FPSAC 2012, pp. 543–554; the current repository page has an inconsistent December 2011 publication field.

references.title: Galois groups of chromatic polynomials
references.venue: LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics
references.annotation: Computes groups for graph families and constructs infinite families with nonsymmetric groups. Its examples also show why groups of separate irreducible factors cannot simply be multiplied.

references.authors: Bohn, Adam and Cameron, Peter J. and Müller, Peter
references.title: Galois groups of multivariate Tutte polynomials
references.annotation: Theorem 1 proves the symmetric-group result for the multivariate Tutte polynomial of a connected matroid. Conjecture 9 asks for the analogous result for the ordinary bivariate Tutte polynomial in characteristic zero.

references.authors: Goodall, Andrew and Jouve, Florent and Sereni, Jean-Sébastien
references.title: On the irreducibility and monodromy of Tutte polynomials
references.annotation: Restates the full symmetric-group conjecture for connected matroids. Theorems 4.5 and 4.7 establish it for cycle graphs and for uniform matroids of fixed rank with sufficiently large ground set. Uniform matroids in all ranks and sizes are not covered by that statement.

references.authors: Merino, Criel and de Mier, Anna and Noy, Marc
references.title: Irreducibility of the Tutte polynomial of a connected matroid
references.venue: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B
references.annotation: Proves Brylawski’s irreducibility conjecture for connected matroids. This supplies transitivity over the rational function field, but does not determine the full Galois group.

references.title: Moduli Spaces of Quadratic Maps: Arithmetic and Geometry
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Relates irreducibility of quadratic Gleason polynomials over Q to geometric irreducibility of curves of quadratic rational maps with a periodic critical point.

references.authors: Benedetto, Robert L. and Goksel, Vefa
references.title: Misiurewicz polynomials and dynamical units, part II
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: States precise Misiurewicz irreducibility and non-unit conjectures, with the necessary root-of-unity normalization and known cases.

references.authors: Benedetto, Robert L. and Goksel, Vefa
references.title: The non-unit conjecture for Misiurewicz parameters
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Proves further non-unit results under explicit irreducibility assumptions. The introduction records the unresolved irreducibility problem and distinguishes values of polynomials from differences of individual parameters.
references.metadata_note: Published 25 June 2026; theorem locators checked in author preprint v2.

references.title: On postcritically finite unicritical polynomials
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Studies critical-parameter polynomials and disproves unrestricted higher-degree Gleason irreducibility: period three has a cyclotomic factor when the degree is 1 modulo 6.

references.authors: Baker, Matthew and Chen, Andrea and Li, Sophie and Qian, Matthew
references.title: Necklaces, permutations, and periodic critical orbits for quadratic polynomials
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Gives bijections connecting real critical parameters and factorization of Gleason polynomials modulo 2. The introduction retains the rational irreducibility conjecture.

references.authors: DeMark, David and Hindes, Wade and Jones, Rafe and Misplon, Moses and Stoll, Michael and Stoneman, Michael
references.title: Eventually stable quadratic polynomials over Q
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Studies reciprocal-integer quadratic parameters. Conjectures 1.7 and 1.8 predict at most four factors and detection of stability at the second iterate.

references.title: A finiteness theorem for specializations of dynatomic polynomials
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Proves that rational specializations with smaller-than-generic dynatomic Galois group are finite for periods 5, 6, 7, and 9. The exceptional parameters are not explicitly determined.

references.title: Irreducibility and Galois groups of truncated binomial polynomials
references.annotation: Proves explicit ranges of irreducibility and conditional effective bounds for binomial truncations.

references.title: Reducibility and irreducibility of Stern (0,1)-polynomials
references.annotation: Studies Stern (0,1)-polynomials and states four factorization conjectures in §8.

references.title: Zeros of Stern polynomials in the complex plane
references.annotation: Proves a zero-free disk and prime-index irreducibility for the Klavžar–Milutinović–Petr Stern sequence; records a half-plane conjecture.

references.title: Newman polynomials, reducibility, and roots on the unit circle
references.annotation: States the five-term reducibility conjecture and relates cyclotomic factors to roots on the unit circle.

references.authors: Koley, Biswajit and Reddy Arikatla, Satyanarayana
references.title: Cyclotomic factors of Borwein polynomials
references.venue: Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society
references.annotation: Proves Mercer’s cyclotomic-divisor classification; keeps the stronger reducibility conjecture separate.

references.title: Galois groups of binom(n,0) + binom(n,1)X + ⋯ + binom(n,6)X⁶
references.annotation: Proves that only finitely many sextic binomial truncations have group other than S₆, using a resolvent curve and Faltings’ theorem. Credits the earlier result of Rouse and Juillerat and restates the conjecture for every n≥11.

references.title: Widely Digitally Stable Numbers and Irreducibility Criteria for Polynomials With Prime Values
references.venue: University of South Carolina, doctoral dissertation
references.annotation: The second part proves finiteness of exceptional sextic binomial Galois groups. Klahn–Technau credit Rouse and Juillerat and cite Theorem 1.3. The repository abstract was checked; the full dissertation was not accessible in this review.

references.authors: von zur Gathen, Joachim and Nöcker, Michael
references.title: Polynomial and Normal Bases for Finite Fields
references.section: Finite fields: construction and prescribed coefficients
references.annotation: Studies finite-field arithmetic using sparse polynomial bases and normal bases. Conjectures 2.5 and 2.8 predict bounded-weight irreducible polynomials and irreducible polynomials x^n+h with deg h at most 3+log_q n. The author-hosted prepublication text retains these locators.

references.title: Galois groups of random polynomials over the rational function field
references.venue: Journal of the London Mathematical Society
references.annotation: For fixed odd q and fixed d≥1, proves that a monic polynomial of increasing degree with independent uniform coefficients of degree at most d in F_q[t] has group S_n with probability tending to one conditional on irreducibility. This removes the Chowla hypothesis in the earlier odd-characteristic result.
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.metadata_note: Corollary 1.1 and Remark 1.4 checked in author text arXiv v2 (22 November 2024). The odd-characteristic assumption is absent from the abstract but explicit in the theorem.

references.title: Experimental evidence for Maeda’s conjecture on modular forms
references.annotation: States Maeda’s conjecture and verifies T_2 through weight 14000 using modular factorizations; Theorem 1.5 gives the precise range of other Hecke indices.

references.title: A possible generalization of Maeda’s conjecture
references.annotation: Questions 2.1–2.3 concern boundedness, stabilization and multiplicativity of Galois orbit counts at fixed level. Distinguishes CM from non-CM forms.
references.venue: Computations with Modular Forms, Contributions in Mathematical and Computational Sciences 6
references.status: Published chapter; question locators checked in arXiv v1 (2012)

references.authors: Banerjee, Debargha and Das, Dhrubajyoti and Das, Srijan and Mandal, Tathagata and Mondal, Sudipa
references.title: Towards a generalized Maeda conjecture for modular forms with quadratic nebentypus
references.annotation: Studies local invariants and lower bounds on non-CM Galois orbit counts. The introduction records the still-conjectural fixed-level picture; the paper does not settle Maeda’s conjecture.

references.title: An application of Maeda’s conjecture to the inverse Galois problem
references.annotation: Shows, conditionally on Maeda’s conjecture, that PSL_2(F_(p^r)) occurs over Q ramified only at p, for each positive even r and a density-one set of primes p.

references.title: Irreducibility of the zero polynomials of Eisenstein series
references.annotation: Proves irreducibility for weights 12·2^ℓ by coefficient-valuation estimates and Dumas’ criterion. The full all-weight conjecture remains distinct from this infinite subfamily.
references.status: Published article; theorem checked in arXiv v1

references.title: Lacunary recurrences and 2-adic properties of Eisenstein series
references.annotation: Reports a proof of González’s minimal 2-adic coefficient-valuation conjecture. This is a related advance, not a proof of the general irreducibility conjecture for Eisenstein zero polynomials.

references.authors: Browning, Tim and Gundlach, Fabian and Sawin, Will
references.title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
references.group: Counting, random polynomials, and random matrices
references.status: Preprint; submitted 13 October 2026; abstract and primary bibliographic records verified
references.annotation: Studies integer matrices with a prescribed monic characteristic polynomial. The abstract reports a bound uniform in the polynomial and improving earlier bounds for matrix size at least four. The full paper was not retrievable in this review; no exact bound is asserted here.

references.title: The arithmetic of curves defined by iteration
references.section: Iteration, composition, and arboreal Galois groups
references.annotation: Relates quadratic-iterate Galois groups to rational points on curves. The final discussion asks a uniform finite-level maximality question, including the proposed level-four bound.

references.section: Special families: Bernoulli and Euler polynomials
references.title: On mth order Bernoulli polynomials of degree m that are Eisenstein
references.annotation: Proves a positive lower density greater than one-fifth of Eisenstein diagonal Bernoulli polynomials. Page 22 states Adelberg’s conjecture for even n and the quotient by x−n/2 for odd n.

references.section: Special families: Bernoulli and Euler polynomials
references.title: Higher Order Bernoulli Polynomials and Newton Polygons
references.annotation: Studies higher-order Bernoulli factorization through Newton polygons. Original source of the diagonal irreducibility conjecture, restated by Adelberg–Filaseta in 2002.
references.metadata_note: Publisher metadata checked. The full chapter was not available; the conjecture was checked in the later primary article by Adelberg–Filaseta.

references.section: Special families: Bernoulli and Euler polynomials
references.title: On nth order Euler polynomials of degree n that are Eisenstein
references.annotation: Gives an exact odd-prime Eisenstein criterion for diagonal higher-order Euler polynomials and lower density at least (log 2)/2. The introduction states that the same argument improves the diagonal Bernoulli lower bound to (log 2)/2. These are order-n families, not ordinary Appell polynomials.
